title: Switching to the flugelhorn
summary: After work on her teeth she took to the flugelhorn, citing Miles Davis and Clark Terry, and carried it around hoping to play.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Well, it's too bad that that was discouraging.
But, in fact, you didn't, you (indistinct) got a flueghorn.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Well I practiced for awhile, then I had to have some work done on my teeth. And that's what kept me away from the horn. And by the time my mouth got well enough for me to play, and I looked at myself in the mirror with this horn -- and you couldn't see me for the horn -- I thought I'd try to find something a little smaller. And, of course, the flügel horn was coming in to popularity by some of the reed man, so I decided I'd get a flügel horn.

Right. And they weren't necessarily playing a whole lot of high notes. I was afraid of those high notes, you know, that trumpet players are expected to play. I could just see my eyes popping out. So I got a flügal horn, and I practiced the

So then, after I started back singing
again, I used to take the horn around with me hoping
somebody would want to know what's in that box so
I could take it out and play it.

I believed I saw you
play the flügal horn around 1969, or whenever it
